# Synthetic recovery fixtures

`all-types.hc22000` and `oracle.json` are generated by `../make_fixtures.py`.
The password is `labpass42`. All addresses, nonces and traffic are synthetic.
There are 37 records: PMKID SHA1/SHA256, EAPOL descriptor versions 1/2/3,
all six message-pair values, FT PMKID/EAPOL, both nonce correction byte orders,
empty/binary SSIDs and a long EAPOL packet. Python hashlib/hmac implements the
reference derivations independently of Windows BCrypt and our OpenCL kernels.
The small Python AES/CMAC oracle checks published known-answer vectors first.

`converter-export.hc22000` contains 12 synthetic interoperability records
originally produced by the project maintainers' capture converter. Its password
is `synthetic-test-password`. The fixture is self-contained and covers
TKIP/CCMP-128/GCMP-128 output; no converter installation is required.

`hashcat-public.hc22000` is the public self-test vector from
[Hashcat v8.0.0 module_22000.c](https://github.com/hashcat/hashcat/blob/v8.0.0/src/modules/module_22000.c).
The upstream MIT license is retained in `../../third_party/hashcat/LICENSE.txt`.
Its password is `hashcat!`. This fixture is test data, not a captured user network.

Cryptographic references:

- [RFC 4493: AES-CMAC](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4493)
- [RFC 4231: HMAC-SHA256](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4231)
- [RFC 2202: HMAC-MD5 and HMAC-SHA1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2202)
- [FIPS 197: AES](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/197/final)

Do not replace these fixtures with live captures or recovered private passwords.
